messages.subject: post-stratifying by forest type in point transect sampling
parts:
Hello team (again)

I have what I hope will be my final problem with Distance analysis.

My data set contains 10 point transects; 5 of the points are located entirely in pristine forest (both the EDR and all observations), 1 is entirely in the regenerating forest, and 4 feature both forest types within the EDR.

I have attached an example of one of the mixed forest points. The point transect ‘E’ is in the middle, and on the left is the regenerating forest with three observations within it (E5, E6, and E7).

My problem is I cannot figure out how to enter the data so that I can post-stratify by forest type. How do I designate the ‘pristine’ vs. ‘regenerating’ forest within the same point transect in the data import tab in Distance? 

Once again, thank you for your time.

Lauren

messages.author: 8fbbf490c07a1909
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] post-stratifying by forest type in point transect sampling
parts:
Hi Lauren and list

As far as I know, you cannot specify multiple strata for a single sampling unit (transect).  In your example, to get around this you would include forest type at the observation level, not the transect level, which would allow you to post-stratify by forest type.  

Cheers,

Stewart

parts:
Hi Stewart,

Thanks for your reply. This is how I ended up entering the data in Distance, and the results seem to make sense (for now):

I divided locations that had both forest types into two different points. For example, a point that was initially 2.08 square kilometres with 9 groups became two points, 1.36 and .72 square kilometres with 6 and 3 groups, respectively. Consequently I have 12 point transects instead of 10. I added the 'forest type' label as a third 'region' column after 'label' and 'area'. I realize this will have implications for the detection function at 0m in the regenerating forest, but I needed to know the density within the specific forest type, rather than within the entire survey area. I hope this makes sense. 

Thanks again for your help,
Lauren
